verses.zh: 约沙法大有尊荣资财，就与亚哈结亲。
verses.en: Jehoshaphat was very wealthy and greatly respected. He made an alliance by marriage with Ahab,

verses.zh: 过了几年，他下到撒马利亚去见亚哈；亚哈为他和跟从他的人宰了许多牛羊，劝他与自己同去攻取基列的拉末。
verses.en: and after several years[NOTE:1] went down to visit[NOTE:2] Ahab in Samaria.[NOTE:3] Ahab slaughtered many sheep and cattle to honor Jehoshaphat and those who came with him.[NOTE:4] He persuaded him to join in an attack[NOTE:5] against Ramoth Gilead.
notes: Heb “at the end of years.”
The word “visit” is supplied in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
Heb “and Ahab slaughtered for him sheep and cattle in abundance, and for the people who were with him.”
Heb “to go up.”

verses.zh: 以色列王亚哈问犹大王约沙法说：「你肯同我去攻取基列的拉末吗？」他回答说：「你我不分彼此，我的民与你的民一样，必与你同去争战。」
verses.en: King Ahab of Israel said to King Jehoshaphat of Judah, “Will you go with me to attack Ramoth Gilead?” He replied, “I will support you; my army is at your disposal and will support you in battle.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Like me, like you; and like your people, my people; and with you in battle.”

verses.zh: 约沙法对以色列王说：「请你先求问耶和华。」
verses.en: Then Jehoshaphat said further to the king of Israel,[NOTE:1] “First,[NOTE:2] please seek an oracle from the Lord.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The word “further” has been added on the basis that this is a second speech act. The narrator uses the title “king of Israel” to convey a sense of formality.
Or “even today,” “right away.”

Heb “inquire for the Lord’s message.” Jehoshaphat is requesting a prophetic oracle revealing the Lord’s will in the matter and their prospects for success. For examples of such oracles, see 2 Sam 5:19, 23-24.

verses.zh: 于是以色列王招聚先知四百人，问他们说：「我们上去攻取基列的拉末可以不可以？」他们说：「可以上去，因为　神必将那城交在王的手里。」
verses.en: So the king of Israel assembled 400 prophets and asked them, “Should we attack Ramoth Gilead or not?”[NOTE:1] They said, “Attack! God[NOTE:2] will hand it over to the king.”
notes: Heb “Should we go against Ramoth Gilead for war or should I refrain?”

Though Jehoshaphat had requested an oracle from “the Lord” (יְהוָה, yehvah, “Yahweh”), the Israelite prophets stop short of actually using this name and substitute the title הָאֱלֹהִים (haʾelohim, “the God”). This ambiguity may explain in part Jehoshaphat’s hesitancy and caution (vv. 7-8). He seems to doubt that the 400 are genuine prophets of the Lord.

verses.zh: 约沙法说：「这里不是还有耶和华的先知，我们可以求问他吗？」
verses.en: But Jehoshaphat asked, “Is there not a prophet of the Lord still here that we may ask him?”

verses.zh: 以色列王对约沙法说：「还有一个人，是音拉的儿子米该雅。我们可以托他求问耶和华，只是我恨他；因为他指着我所说的预言，不说吉语，常说凶言。」约沙法说：「王不必这样说。」
verses.en: The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, “There is still one man through whom we can seek the Lord’s will,[NOTE:1] but I despise[NOTE:2] him because he does not prophesy prosperity for me, but always[NOTE:3] disaster—Micaiah son of Imlah.” Jehoshaphat said, “The king should not say such things!”
notes: Heb “to seek the Lord from him.”
Or “hate.”
Heb “all his days.”

verses.zh: 以色列王就召了一个太监来，说：「你快去将音拉的儿子米该雅召来。」
verses.en: The king of Israel summoned an officer and said, “Quickly bring Micaiah son of Imlah.”

verses.zh: 以色列王和犹大王约沙法在撒马利亚城门前的空场上，各穿朝服坐在位上，所有的先知都在他们面前说预言。
verses.en: Now the king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah were sitting on their respective thrones, dressed in their royal robes, at the threshing floor at[NOTE:1] the entrance of the gate of Samaria. All the prophets were prophesying before them.
notes: Heb “at,” which in this case probably means “near.”

verses.zh: 基拿拿的儿子西底家造了两个铁角，说：「耶和华如此说：『你要用这角抵触亚兰人，直到将他们灭尽。』」
verses.en: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah made iron horns and said, “This is what the Lord says, ‘With these you will gore Syria until they are destroyed.’”

verses.zh: 所有的先知也都这样预言说：「可以上基列的拉末去，必然得胜，因为耶和华必将那城交在王的手中。」
verses.en: All the prophets were prophesying the same, saying, “Attack Ramoth Gilead! You will succeed; the Lord will hand it over to the king.”

verses.zh: 那去召米该雅的使者对米该雅说：「众先知一口同音地都向王说吉言，你不如与他们说一样的话，也说吉言。」
verses.en: Now the messenger who went to summon Micaiah said to him, “Look, the prophets are in complete agreement that the king will succeed.[NOTE:1] Your words must agree with theirs; you must predict success!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the words of the prophets are [with] one mouth good for the king.”
Heb “let your words be like one of them and speak good.”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「我指着永生的耶和华起誓，我的　神说甚么，我就说甚么。」
verses.en: But Micaiah said, “As certainly as the Lord lives, I will say what my God tells me to say!”

verses.zh: 米该雅到王面前，王问他说：「米该雅啊，我们上去攻取基列的拉末可以不可以？」他说：「可以上去，必然得胜，敌人必交在你们手里。」
verses.en: Micaiah[NOTE:1] came before the king and the king asked him, “Micaiah, should we attack Ramoth Gilead or not?” He answered him, “Attack! You will succeed; they will be handed over to you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Micaiah) has been specified in the translation both for clarity and for stylistic reasons.

One does not expect Micaiah, having just vowed to speak only what the Lord tells him, to agree with the other prophets and give the king an inaccurate prophecy. Micaiah’s actions became understandable later, when we discover that the Lord desires to deceive the king and lead him to his demise. The Lord even dispatches a lying spirit to deceive Ahab’s prophets. Micaiah can lie to the king because he realizes this lie is from the Lord. It is important to note that in v. 13 Micaiah only vows to speak the word of his God; he does not necessarily say he will tell the truth. In this case the Lord’s word is deliberately deceptive. Only when the king adjures him to tell the truth (v. 15), does Micaiah do so.

verses.zh: 王对他说：「我当嘱咐你几次，你才奉耶和华的名向我说实话呢？」
verses.en: The king said to him, “How many times must I make you solemnly promise in[NOTE:1] the name of the Lord to tell me only the truth?”
notes: Or “swear an oath by.”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「我看见以色列众民散在山上，如同没有牧人的羊群一般。耶和华说：『这民没有主人，他们可以平平安安地各归各家去。』」
verses.en: Micaiah[NOTE:1] replied, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains like sheep that have no shepherd. Then the Lord said, ‘They have no master. They should go home in peace.’”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Micaiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 以色列王对约沙法说：「我岂没有告诉你，这人指着我所说的预言，不说吉语，单说凶言吗？」
verses.en: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “Didn’t I tell you he does not prophesy prosperity for me, but disaster?”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「你们要听耶和华的话。我看见耶和华坐在宝座上，天上的万军侍立在他左右。
verses.en: Micaiah[NOTE:1] said, “That being the case, listen to the Lord’s message. I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, with all the heavenly assembly standing on his right and on his left.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Micaiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶和华说：『谁去引诱以色列王亚哈上基列的拉末去阵亡呢？』这个就这样说，那个就那样说。
verses.en: The Lord said, ‘Who will deceive King Ahab of Israel, so he will attack Ramoth Gilead and die there?’ One said this and another that.

verses.zh: 随后，有一个神灵出来，站在耶和华面前说：『我去引诱他。』耶和华问他说：『你用何法呢？』
verses.en: Then a spirit[NOTE:1] stepped forward and stood before the Lord. He said, ‘I will deceive him.’ The Lord asked him, ‘How?’
notes: Heb “the spirit.” The significance of the article prefixed to רוּחַ (ruakh) is uncertain, but it could contain a clue as to this spirit’s identity, especially when interpreted in light of verse 23. It is certainly possible, and probably even likely, that the article is used in a generic or dramatic sense and should be translated, “a spirit.” In the latter case it would show that this spirit was vivid and definite in the mind of Micaiah the storyteller. However, if one insists that the article indicates a well-known or universally known spirit, the following context provides a likely referent. Verse 23 tells how Zedekiah slapped Micaiah in the face and then asked sarcastically, “Which way did the spirit from the Lord (רוּחַ־יְהוָה, ruakh yehvah) go when he went from me to speak to you?” When the phrase “the spirit of the Lord” refers to the divine spirit (rather than the divine breath or mind, as in Isa 40:7, 13) elsewhere, the spirit energizes an individual or group for special tasks or moves one to prophesy. This raises the possibility that the deceiving spirit of vv. 20-22 is the same as the divine spirit mentioned by Zedekiah in v. 23. This would explain why the article is used on רוּחַ (ruakh); he can be called “the spirit” because he is the well-known spirit who energizes the prophets.

verses.zh: 他说：『我去，要在他众先知口中作谎言的灵。』耶和华说：『这样，你必能引诱他，你去如此行吧！』
verses.en: He replied, ‘I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets.’ The Lord[NOTE:1] said, ‘Deceive and overpower him.[NOTE:2] Go out and do as you have proposed.’
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The Hebrew text has two imperfects connected by וְגַם (vegam). These verbs could be translated as specific futures, “you will deceive and also you will prevail,” in which case the Lord is assuring the spirit of success on his mission. However, in a commissioning context (note the following imperatives) such as this, it is more likely that the imperfects are injunctive, in which case one could translate, “Deceive, and also overpower.”

verses.zh: 现在耶和华使谎言的灵入了你这些先知的口，并且耶和华已经命定降祸与你。」
verses.en: So now, look, the Lord has placed a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of yours, but the Lord has decreed disaster for you.”

verses.zh: 基拿拿的儿子西底家前来打米该雅的脸，说：「耶和华的灵从哪里离开我与你说话呢？」
verses.en: Zedekiah son of Kenaanah approached, hit Micaiah on the jaw, and said, “Which way did the Lord’s Spirit go when he went from me to speak to you?”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「你进严密的屋子藏躲的那日，就必看见了。」
verses.en: Micaiah replied, “Look, you will see in the day when you go into an inner room to hide.”

verses.zh: 以色列王说：「将米该雅带回，交给邑宰亚们和王的儿子约阿施，说：
verses.en: Then the king of Israel said, “Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the city official and Joash the king’s son.

verses.zh: 『王如此说：把这个人下在监里，使他受苦，吃不饱喝不足，等候我平平安安地回来。』」
verses.en: Say, ‘This is what the king says: “Put this man in prison. Give him only a little bread and water[NOTE:1] until I return safely.”’”
notes: Heb “the bread of affliction and the water of affliction.”

verses.zh: 米该雅说：「你若能平安回来，那就是耶和华没有藉我说这话了」；又说：「众民哪，你们都要听！」
verses.en: Micaiah said, “If you really do return safely, then the Lord has not spoken through me!” Then he added, “Take note,[NOTE:1] all you people.”
notes: Heb “Listen.”

verses.zh: 以色列王和犹大王约沙法上基列的拉末去了。
verses.en: The king of Israel and King Jehoshaphat of Judah attacked Ramoth Gilead.

verses.zh: 以色列王对约沙法说：「我要改装上阵，你可以仍穿王服。」于是以色列王改装，他们就上阵去了。
verses.en: The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself and then enter[NOTE:1] the battle, but you wear your royal attire.” So the king of Israel disguised himself and they entered the battle.
notes: The Hebrew verbal forms could be imperatives (“Disguise yourself and enter”), but this would make no sense in light of the immediately following context. The forms are better interpreted as infinitives absolute functioning as cohortatives (see IBHS 594 §35.5.2a). Some prefer to emend the forms to imperfects.

verses.zh: 先是亚兰王吩咐车兵长说：「他们的兵将，无论大小，你们都不可与他们争战，只要与以色列王争战。」
verses.en: Now the king of Syria had ordered his chariot commanders, “Do not fight common soldiers or high ranking officers;[NOTE:1] fight only the king of Israel!”
notes: Heb “small or great.”

verses.zh: 车兵长看见约沙法便说，这必是以色列王，就转过去与他争战。约沙法一呼喊，耶和华就帮助他，　神又感动他们离开他。
verses.en: When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, “He must be the king of Israel!” So they turned and attacked him, but Jehoshaphat cried out. The Lord helped him; God lured them away from him.

verses.zh: 车兵长见不是以色列王，就转去不追他了。
verses.en: When the chariot commanders realized he was not the king of Israel, they turned away from him.

verses.zh: 有一人随便开弓，恰巧射入以色列王的甲缝里。王对赶车的说：「我受了重伤，你转过车来，拉我出阵吧！」
verses.en: Now an archer shot an arrow at random,[NOTE:1] and it struck the king of Israel between the plates of his armor. The king[NOTE:2] ordered his charioteer, “Turn around and take me from the battle line,[NOTE:3] for I am wounded.”
notes: Heb “now a man drew a bow in his innocence” (i.e., with no specific target in mind, or at least without realizing his target was the king of Israel).
Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “camp.”

verses.zh: 那日阵势越战越猛，以色列王勉强站在车上抵挡亚兰人，直到晚上。约在日落的时候，王就死了。
verses.en: While the battle raged throughout the day, the king of Israel stood propped up in his chariot opposite the Syrians. He died in the evening as the sun was setting.
